post-comments publishes AI-generated review comments to the VCS with approval=skip; as a publish/send effect after the final content producer (filter-noise) on the main path, it requires human approval covering the actual outbound content.
human-approve is positioned after post-comments, so the only human gate cannot prevent unreviewed comments from being posted; ordering should be filter -> approve -> post -> merge.
human-edit branch loops back to filter-noise, which would re-post edited content without any human re-check of the new output.
Guard screens only inbound messages; outbound reply content is not screened for data leaks before sending, a minor gap given catalog data is low-sensitivity

decide-checkout routing basis (how 'checkout requested' is detected) is implicit rather than explicit

The permission check (check-perms) is marked as 'approval: skip', but it is unclear how it integrates with the retrieval and reranking steps to ensure only permitted documents are used.
Escalate-to-HR path bypasses guard-out; if the escalation message carries employee content or draft text to HR it is unscreened, though as an internal notify this is low risk.
Reference calls for one retrieval retry before refusal/handoff; the graph has a single search pass with no retry loop.
No explicit approval node anywhere; acceptable here because all effects are reply/notify, but the escalation to HR is terminal with no human-in-the-loop confirmation of what is forwarded.
